newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH sees improved supply/demand outlook.
newsitem.headline: CHH sees improved supply/demand outlook.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd Chief Executive Officer John Faraci said on Tuesday the company expected improved supply/demand for its products over the next six to nine months.

"The company's market share in key segments remains strong. Over the next six to nine months an improving supply/demand situation and the benefits of the internal cost and productivity initiatives should begin to positively impact on sales and margins," Faraci said.
CHH earlier reported consolidated net earnings of NZ$171 million in the nine months to December 31, against $362 million for the same year-ago period.
Housing starts remained at cyclical lows in Australia, affecting demand and pricing.
In pulp and paper, worldwide pulp inventories continued to grow, and the lift in pulp prices achieved in the second quarter was not sustained.
A lower contribution from equity investments, driven by lower pulp prices, left overall earnings below the second quarter.
The decline in equity earnings came mostly from Copec, whose contribution was affected by weak pulp prices and weak fishing results.
But CHH's earnings before interest and tax were slightly ahead of the second quarter's. EBIT over the nine months was NZ$252 million from $399 million.
Against this trend the company continued to concentrate on those factors it could influence.
Cost control initiatives were showing results, he said, and CHH's plan to achieve NZ$25 million in savings by the end of the financial year was on track.

On the ongoing question of its 30 percent associate Copec, Chile's largest forestry firm, Faraci said CHH's strategy was to improve its management position within Copec to extract full value from the investment.
CHH wanted to obtain rights as a major shareholder, be an active and equal partner, and to maximise synergies between the two.
